- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if recent history shows downward momentum.
- If model shows sharp spikes (e.g., >3x recent mean) in 30d forecast, it often overshoots; cap or dampen such spikes unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to adjust; check for lagged correction in 10–15d window.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d forecasts when sentiment is volatile; if forecast deviates >1.5σ from recent 18d mean, adjust toward historical range.
- For horizon 30d, if true outcome shows early drop (e.g., first 5 days) after a spike, model often fails to anticipate; reduce early forecast values if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or -0.33, model tends to underreact; increase forecast mid-period if recent price is stable or trending up.
